- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward — overcorrecting or lagging mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, particularly when true prices show strong upward momentum.
- Forecast exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, suggesting model may be overly confident in short-term volatility or misaligned with actual market sentiment.
- Model fails to capture downward momentum in the last 5–10 days when true prices show a clear decline — underestimates risk of correction.
- Model often overreacts to recent price spikes, leading to exaggerated upward forecasts that don’t align with subsequent mean reversion.
- Model underestimates the impact of seasonal or macroeconomic factors — e.g., in April 2025, model missed a strong upward trend due to ignoring policy or supply-demand shifts.
- Model shows inconsistent lag in responding to true price changes — especially when true prices dip, model takes 2–3 days to adjust downward.
